analyst_notes: The skill achieves 100% pass rate vs 60% baseline — a 40-point improvement
The biggest skill advantage is on structured output: standardized 5-dimension /25 scoring, comparison tables with preview links, consistent presentation format across all modes
Baseline runs invented ad-hoc scoring systems (star ratings, 10-point scales, qualitative high/medium/low) that vary across evals — inconsistent for a production pipeline
The skill correctly flags archival assets (FDR 1941) as unsuitable for stock libraries and provides specific alternative sourcing paths — baseline only mentions this in passing
Treatment survivability scoring (the skill's key differentiator) produces actionable guidance ('duotone gold' vs 'low survivability') that the baseline approximates but doesn't systematize
Cost: skill runs use ~23% more tokens and ~6% more time. Acceptable overhead for the output quality improvement.
Baseline eval-1 and eval-2 saved outputs to wrong directories — possible sign that without structured workflow, agents are less disciplined about file organization
Non-discriminating assertion: 'Generates reasonable search terms' passes trivially in both configurations — consider replacing with a more specific assertion about term specificity/fallback strategy
